text:
mike: idea — instead of evicting individual prefixes purely by recency/hotness, group prefixes into similarity clusters (based on recent token sequences / prefix fingerprints) and evict/soft-demote at the cluster level. can reduce churn for prompt families that share KV. curious about correctness risks and migration.
ana: sketch? cluster boundary, size, and update cadence will matter. are you thinking offline clusters or online streaming LSH-style? :thinking_face:
devon: two quick concerns: i) cross-tenant leakage if clusters span tenants (we must keep tenant isolation). ii) versioning keys when cluster membership changes — we could end up with duplicate kv entries pointing to same logical state.
mike: good call on tenant isolation — proposal is per-tenant clustering by default. optionally a shared global cluster if tenant opts in. for membership, cluster id is a stable epoched id. when keys move clusters, we write a tombstone mapping from old cluster->new cluster for short period.
kari: tombstones + mapping is doable, but increases lookup latency. what's the expected perf win vs overhead? any sim data?
mike: rough sim on sampled traces: cluster-level eviction reduced redundant fetches ~15% and reduced async prefetch churn ~22% for a chat-heavy product. latency delta in lookups was +0.6ms on p99 in the sim (mainly due to cluster indirection). net token cost down ~8%.
ana: that p99 hit is worrying. can we do lazy mapping lookup: first try direct key->value, only consult cluster-index on miss? most hits will be local and avoid extra hop.
devon: lazy mapping is safer. also we should keep an LRU per cluster to avoid evicting the whole cluster at once — graceful demotion policy: mark cluster as "cooling" and gradually demote members based on internal recency.
mike: agreed — cluster cooling + per-member decay. also a soft-evict threshold: move to compressed/quantized resident format rather than full eviction if cluster is frequently reactivated.
kari: compressed resident format promising. what's the quantization plan? 8-bit vs 4-bit? hardware profile differs across Dedicated vs Private.
mike: defaults: 8-bit for hosted, 4-bit optional for Dedicated with verification. conversion is async and served via fallback path until complete.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: FYI there's a running canary for kv-prefetch 3 in zone us-west-2 (build 2026.03.19-rc). No impact expected.
ana: on correctness: we must ensure read-after-write for pinned prefixes. pinned prefixes should bypass cluster-level demotion entirely.
devon: also consider causal consistency during cluster rebalance. If a writer moves a prefix into a new cluster while readers are still routed to the old cluster id, we need a fast forwarding mechanism.
mike: plan: cluster rebalance uses a two-phase switch. phase 1: copy pointer and add forwarding entry old->new, phase 2: cut over and garbage collect old entries once no inflight leases reference them. forwarding entries carry a monotonically increasing epoch to detect stale reads.
kari: two-phase sounds right. but garbage collection is tricky for long-lived leases. maybe GC after X wall time + when lease refcounts drop to zero.
ana: testing: let's add a canary layer that simulates 1% of traffic using cluster logic and record regressions on p50/p95/p99 + miss amplification + extra lookups.
devon: add correctness checks: invariant tests that verify RA-write for pinned keys, and a chaos test that rebalances clusters while doing concurrent writes/reads.
mike: rollout plan: 1) simulate offline on historical traces and fine-tune cluster size & cooling params. 2) opt-in canary (1% traffic), collect metrics. 3) ramp to 20% with fallback toggle. 4) full roll with default off for older clusters.
ana: what about telemetry? need per-cluster metrics: hit rate, eviction rate, remap count, average mapping latency, and cluster reactivation frequency.
kari: plus a metric for tombstone bounce (how often lookups hit a tombstone redirect) and wall-clock time until GC.
devon: open question: how to represent cluster id in the KV keyspace without bloating key length. suggestions?
mike: compact encoding: 64-bit key = hash(prefix) ^ (cluster_epoch << 48) or use separate small index table mapping cluster_id -> shard. want to avoid changing on-wire protocol though.
ana: prefer separate index table keyed by prefix-hash -> (cluster_id, epoch) so existing on-disk KV keys remain stable. index lookup is a tiny in-memory table per node.
kari: ok do that. ops question: will this increase memory pressure? index needs to be memory-efficient — use cuckoo/hash with eviction for very stale prefixes.
devon: concurrency model for updates must avoid global locks: use compare-and-swap on index entries and epoch monotonic check.
mike: I'll draft a short RFC with: definition, API changes (pin bypass, tombstone mapping), cluster placement algorithm, metrics and canary plan, rollout, test harness. aiming for PR by EOW.
ana: nice. add a section on multi-model shared prefixes (different model variants reusing same prefix momentum) and how we tag clusters with model compatibility labels.
kari: also mention fallback to per-prefix eviction if cluster logic fails or p99 regression exceeds threshold — automatic rollback toggle.
infra-bot: alert-bot: created issue KV-4672: "cluster-eviction-proposal: RFC + canary plan" assigned to mike.
mike: thanks — i'll post RFC link here when ready. short follow-ups: can someone volunteer to baseline current miss amplification numbers this week?
devon: i'll take baseline. will post numbers in #eng-runtime by Thu.
kari: I'll help define the metrics dashboard tiles.
ana: I'll review the RFC once posted.
mike: awesome — thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
